chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Buzayʿ narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from Sulaymān ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, for the nutfah there are twenty dinars, for the ʿalaqah forty dinars, for the muḍghah sixty dinars, and for the bone eighty dinars. Then when it is clothed with flesh, it is one hundred. Then it remains one hundred until it cries out, and when it cries out, the diyyah is complete.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Financial blood-money compensation due for injury or killing.
key_terms.النُّطْفَةِ: The sperm-drop or earliest embryonic stage.
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةِ: The clinging clot stage of embryonic development.
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: The chewed-like lump stage of the embryo.
key_terms.دِينَاراً: A dinar; the monetary unit used here for legal compensation.
key_terms.كَامِلَةً: Complete or full, meaning the full amount of diyyah.

ai.seo_question: What blood money is due for a fetus at different stages of development in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out staged blood-money amounts for the developing fetus, assigning increasing compensation as it advances from nutfah to ʿalaqah, muḍghah, bone, and then flesh-covered form. Once the newborn cries out, the full diyyah becomes due, indicating a complete legal status in this ruling.
